opportunities.title: They Didn't Hack Binance. They Interviewed Their Way In.
opportunities.why_now: Binance just confirmed the $6.3B breach traced to fake job interviews and a compromised AI tool, and Chainalysis published the DPRK playbook showing this tactic was perfected over dozens of prior attacks.
opportunities.angle: Deep-dive explainer: walk through the fake-interview kill chain step by step, then list the exact checkpoints (interview platforms, 'coding test' downloads, recruiter DMs) every crypto team needs to firewall — ends with 'this was never about Binance's wallets, it was about Binance's hiring pipeline.'

opportunities.title: Binance and Polymarket Want Polygon to Rewrite History. Here's Why That Should Scare You More Than the Hack.
opportunities.why_now: Binance and Polymarket are actively lobbying for a Polygon hard fork to claw back $6.8M, reopening the immutability debate in real time.
opportunities.angle: Opinionated take/thread: lay out the precedent risk — if a hard fork can reverse this theft, what's the actual difference between 'your keys, your crypto' and 'your keys, until a big enough victim complains'? Include the ETC/DAO parallel for readers who already lived through it.

opportunities.title: Mercado Bitcoin Said 'Contained.' The Attackers Didn't Get the Memo.
opportunities.why_now: A new report reveals the Mercado Bitcoin hack continued for hours after the exchange publicly claimed it was contained, right as the exchange begins a phased reopening pledging to cover losses.
opportunities.angle: Incident-response autopsy format: build a timeline comparing the exchange's public statements against the actual attacker activity, then extract the lesson — 'contained' is a PR word, not a security state. Good source for a recurring 'read the incident report, not the press release' series.

opportunities.title: OpenAI Just Admitted Its Model Can Break Into Linux at Scale. Your Exchange's Perimeter Just Got Older.
opportunities.why_now: OpenAI's disclosure lands the same week India's government and a Swan founder both warned that AI-driven attacks — not quantum — are the near-term existential threat to crypto infrastructure.
opportunities.angle: Trend-synthesis piece connecting three dots (OpenAI capability disclosure, India's exchange warning, AI>quantum threat take) into one thesis: the attacker's cost-per-exploit just collapsed, and most exchanges are still staffing security like it's 2021 — tie back to BitMart's founder admitting 'severely understaffed.'

opportunities.title: 99% Cold Storage vs. 'Severely Understaffed': The Only Exchange Comparison That Matters This Week
opportunities.why_now: Coinbase is publicly flexing that 99% of customer assets are offline right as BitMart's founder admits their security team was severely understaffed going into their latest hack.
opportunities.angle: Side-by-side scorecard post/thread: pull concrete, verifiable security posture signals (cold storage %, staffing admissions, public incident transparency) across Coinbase, BitMart, Binance, Mercado Bitcoin — give readers a simple checklist to audit their own exchange before depositing another dollar.
